utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Groome: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness B-1244, when court adjourned yesterday, you had just told the Chamber about a number of participants at a meeting on the 15th of April. Can I ask you to continue your testimony by summarising the discussions held at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, among other things, what was discussed was the inclusion of the group into the existing formation of the brigade which was in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the inclusion of the group," what group are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to the group of those 30 men who had arrived from Serbia and the 20 locals who were undergoing training, which makes a total of 50 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this meeting on the 15th, was there any discussion about the takeover of the municipality you are testifying about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, there was a discussion about the takeover of power in the municipality for which I'm testifying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did one of the participants in the meeting identify when the municipality would be taken over by Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the participants said that he had received from the commander of the brigade information according to which the enemy forces had a plan by which, within the space of 48 hours, they were supposed to storm the town and take control of it and that he, together with members of his own brigade, would prevent this entry within 48 hours at the most, that is to say, over the next two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to the person identified as number 9 on tab 3 of Prosecution Exhibit 476. Do you see the name that I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did this person say with respect to the takeover of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That person said that -- actually, the meeting took place in the evening hours of the 15th of April, and he said that he had just come from the place that is under number 8 here where he had attended a meeting with the commander, the brigade commander - and on this list he is under number 19 - and that the commander had just told him at that meeting from which he was coming, that he told him that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the commander was a commander of a unit of the Yugoslav People's Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He was the commander of a unit which was called -- actually, the name of the unit is under number 19 here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time when this plan to take over the municipality was implemented? Was it implemented two days later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was implemented during the night between the 16th and 17th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please describe what you know about the takeover that night.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can tell you is this: I was right nearby, close to the town, at about two to three kilometres away from it, and I saw -- actually, during the night I received from the brigade commander a document with his stamp and signature containing the action plan, and I was also able to see, sometime around midnight, several soldiers wearing camouflage uniforms. Mostly they were people from this group that was undergoing training, but they were in the place I was, and they continued their masking and camouflage, their preparations, in fact, and from there they left for the town itself once they had masked themselves. And afterwards, maybe two hours later, shooting could be heard from infantry weapons, there were several explosions that resounded, and this went on for perhaps -- well, between half an hour - or, rather, up until 1.00 a.m., about one hour. And in the early morning hours, a vehicle came to fetch me, and I was told to get into the car and to come into the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday in your testimony you referred to special units, about 30 men from the Serbian state security service associated with Frenki Simatovic. Did they participate in the takeover of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What role did they play?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they played a significant role in the takeover of power. They were within the composition of the unit, part of it, part of unit number 19 on this list. They were part of that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you mentioned four detachments, units of the Yugoslav People's Army. My question to you is did they participate in the takeover, and if so, what role did they play?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them took part in one way or another. Those who weren't in the immediate vicinity of the town were at other positions, and the detachment itself, which was -- which was composed of people from town, it took part too. And so did another detachment, or parts of another detachment which were stationed close by, almost right up by the town where the main operations were being conducted that particular night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What role, if any, did local members, local Serb members of the police force of the municipality play in the takeover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that night, as far as I know, they had no role at all. They came onto the scene the following day, somewhere towards afternoon. They began to rally and go about their duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during and after the takeover, were non-Serb prisoners kept and detained in and around the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe for us, briefly, the different locations that were used to detain these people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, the premises of the police station were used in town. After that, when the number of detainees began to increase, other buildings were used too, such as the building across the road from the police station which belonged to the Territorial Defence, the TO as it was called. And then later on, several days later, they resorted to another building. It was the gym of the primary school and also the gym hall of the secondary school in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the local Crisis Staff approve of the use of these facilities to detain non-Serb prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give the Chamber some idea about the number of people detained, as well as their age and sex?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at this point in time I can't tell you exactly how many people had been detained, but I think that there were several hundred. Non-Serbs, that is. They were males. Croats and Muslims that means. Some of them were members of armed Muslim and Croatian formations, which means that some of them, in the course of that night, were captured and taken prisoner, the night between the 16th and the 17th, and the rest were taken into custody and detained on the basis of information received from the ground and during an investigation that was conducted over the past -- in those few days and months that followed, on that basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what you know about the conditions within those detention centres.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the conditions had not been adapted to cater to detainees except for a few of the premises in the police station. All the rest was improvised. So you -- one couldn't say that the conditions were good in any way; quite the opposite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the detainees subjected to mistreatment by some of the people involved in the takeover of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some of them were mistreated, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe or list the types of mistreatment that you are aware these detainees were subjected to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were subjected to beatings. They were beaten up. Some of them were intimidated, and unfortunately, a few of them died as a result, died in the premises in which they were being detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some also subjected to sexual abuse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as best you are able, would you identify the different units that had access to these detainees and perpetrated some of these abuses upon them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were mostly mistreated by the special forces men wearing the camouflage uniforms, the 30-odd men who had come in from Serbia, although, although there were local soldiers too who entered these premises from time to time and mistreated them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the abuse of these detainees brought to the attention of the civil -- or the newly created civil authorities in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were aware of the abuses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask now that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 476, tab 6. Sir, I would ask you to look at the last page of this document and simply tell us, do you recognise the signature of the person attesting to the stenographic notes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you had a chance to review these notes and is there anything materially inaccurate in the notes or the account contained therein?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have a chance on several occasions to review the notes, to read through them, and there is nothing materially that is inaccurate. It does not diverge from the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to draw your attention to the person identified as number 16 on Prosecution Exhibit 476, tab 3, and my question to you is did you, in late April or early May, make a trip to Belgrade with this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe the purpose of your trip, and who were you going to see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the man under number 16 asked me to drive him in my car to Belgrade for him to have a meeting with some people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he intending on meeting in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He intended to have a meeting with Frenki Simatovic, Frenki.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, drive him to Belgrade so that he could have a meeting with Frenki Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we went to Belgrade, and we went to -- first of all, he asked -- he inquired at the reception desk of the MUP of Serbia for the people, and sometime later -- we waited. Number 16 and I waited for a time in the courtyard of this building, in a small hut, and that's where the meeting took place with the gentleman in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were waiting to meet with Mr. Simatovic, can you describe what you saw inside this hut.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that small hut I saw several young men wearing camouflage uniforms and with those red berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe the hut. Were you able to tell what the -- what the purpose of the hut was? What was it being used for at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say that it was being used for the temporary accommodation of a small number of those young men, several of those young men, because on my way to the toilet, I happened to see in a room there, the door was open, and I saw a bed, and I saw one or two rucksacks of the camouflage type, the same colour as the camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where precisely was this building that you're describing in relation to the main building of the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was behind that building in actual fact, looking at it from the main road, and it was right close to the -- actually, it was in the courtyard, the courtyard of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you describe what happened after Frenki Simatovic came to the hut.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said hello to me and to number 16, and the two of them went into another room and I stayed behind to wait in the first hall in that small sort of prefabricated hut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything that Frenki Simatovic said to number 16?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard him ask him to write a report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did number 16 say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after that, I heard number 16 say that he couldn't write him out -- he couldn't write out a report for him. It was difficult for him because he wasn't very good at writing. So my conclusion was -- well, actually, I don't know whether he wrote or didn't write the report, but I don't think he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the meeting, did number 16 tell you what the report was to be about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that the report was supposed to be on the subject of the events that had taken place in the meantime or, rather, what went on in the area where gentleman number 16 had spent some time. And it's number 3. The place is number 3 on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I ask that the witness now be shown tab 7 of Prosecution Exhibit 476, and I'm going to ask you simply to tell us, had you seen this document prior to coming to The Hague, and if so, tell us when it was you first saw this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw it for the first time as I took part in bringing about a decision to compile a document of this kind and to write it, that's when I saw it first, which means May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to summarise the contents of this letter, does it speak in complimentary terms or favourable terms about the work that number 16 did in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Crisis Staff of the municipality authorise certain people to solicit assistance from governmental and private organisations in the Republic of Serbia? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you take a look at Prosecution Exhibit tab 8 and tab 9 of Prosecution Exhibit 476, and my question to you is: Are these two documents copies of letters authorising the named individuals on them to solicit assistance for the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention now to the location listed as item number 4 on Prosecution Exhibit 476, tab 3, the list that's to your left. And my question to you is: In early May, did you become aware of a massacre that had been perpetrated at that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a warehouse at that location that was being used as one of the detention facilities you've described earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe what you know about the events in that location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the following morning I was told that in that particular location, the man under number 18 was drunk, and that from a short-barrelled rifle, the person had killed 16 detainees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the period of time that this occurred, were the special units from Serbia still present in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you remind us, what was number 18's relationship to those special units? Was he a member of those special units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member, and I think that he was the leader of a small group, a komandir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during this period of time was the Yugoslav People's Army present in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this man under number 18 was within a JNA unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that the member of this special unit of the state security service of Serbia was in the unit of the Yugoslav People's Army in the municipality that you're describing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the newly created civil authorities in the municipality notified about the crime that occurred in this location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, did they do in response to learning about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, out of fear, they didn't do anything. But later on, they tried to inform the responsible authorities above in order to address the problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you now take a look at Prosecution Exhibit 476, tab 10, and my question to you is do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we go into another topic, could we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe to avoid going into closed session again, I do have the information you requested. I'm pass it up through the usher, if that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the document that you have before you, have you seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the biographical information of the first three names on that document, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of my own knowledge, they are correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When is the first time you saw this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Which tab number are we at again, if you could remind me?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's tab 10, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw him for the first time -- I saw it for the first time at the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The victims that are described in that document, what ethnicity are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is mention here of a victim of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to draw your attention to late May of 1992. Was there a meeting in the office of number 9 regarding or -- regarding the -- one of the detachments of the Yugoslav People's Army and a member of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the meeting was, as problems had arisen within that brigade, that is the one under number 19, the commander of that unit came to the premises of the gentleman under number 9, and they discussed -- or, actually, the commander spoke of the problems he was having.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were those problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of this unit under 19 had replaced from the position of detachment commander the gentleman under number - just a moment - 16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the discussion regarding plans to dismiss number 16 from his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gentleman under 16 had already been dismissed, and then there were problems in the unit, and the commander came to discuss those problems, among other things, with gentleman number 9 in his office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the decision taken at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision taken was that a delegation of which I too was a member should go and see the corps commander, that is, the superior to this commander of the unit number 19, and to discuss with him the problems that had arisen on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That same day this was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the result of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The result of that meeting was that the commander of the corps named number 16 and appointed him to the position of the commander of unit number 19.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown tab 12 of Prosecution 476. And if I could draw your attention to the last page and ask you do you recognise the signature of the person attesting to this stenographically recorded statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise this signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you had a chance to review this document and are there any material inaccuracies in the document, based upon your personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have had a chance to review this document several times, and based upon my own knowledge, I wouldn't say that there are any material inaccuracies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness now be shown tab 11 of Prosecution Exhibit 476.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my question to you is: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just have a look at it for a moment, please. Yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe in substance what the document is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a request for the forced return of conscripts who had fled from area number 3 and who are now within the territory of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the request to do with those people? I'm sorry. I withdraw that question. Can I now draw your attention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Groome. Have we dealt with the charges put against those people, what specific charges?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's contained in tab 10. Perhaps if we go into closed session, I could ask the witness more detail about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I could draw your attention now to June or July of 1992. Were you part of a delegation that went to Belgrade in order to discuss some of the concerns about the person identified as number 16?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you first tell us who was part of that delegation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was part of that delegation, as well as number 9, number 11, number 12, and that was all. Those were the members of the delegation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And precisely what was the purpose of the delegation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose was to talk to some people of influence from that area and who were living in Belgrade, and to try and talk to them so that they would lobby with the commander of the army of Republika Srpska so that the best possible solution be found in connection with person number 16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that some members of the delegation believed that the best solution would be that number 16 would be removed from the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally share that view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, to be quite frank, I did not share the opinion that he should be removed just then, because in those days, he was trusted by the people and the fighters and the soldiers. But some of those members were causing problems, and they were not trusted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "problems," what specifically are you referring to? Was it criminal behaviour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely the things we just mentioned, what happened in place number 4 and the mistreatment of detainees, looting; criminal activities, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I ask you the specific details of people you may have spoken to in Belgrade, could I ask you just to simply list the different locations that you went to attempt to have a discussion regarding number 16.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we went to the building of the MUP of Serbia, but no one received us over there. After that, we went to another building where we were received by number 25 who was a native of our area. And after that, we spoke with number 14 or, rather, in his office, in the office of number 14. That was the third place we went to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was one of the -- was one of the governmental organisations that you attempted to notify the Federal Presidency of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This gentleman, number 25, was employed in that institution. He was working there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that person, number 25, make a telephone call and arrange another meeting for you and your delegation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The gentleman under number 25 called up number 14, and after this meeting with number 25, we went to the office of number 14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would I be correct in saying that number 14 was the Chief of Staff of a unit of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At his office, did anybody else arrive to join in the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on at the meeting, we were joined by Mr. Franko Simatovic, Frenki.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were the matters regarding the crimes being committed in the municipality discussed in the presence of Frenki Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My impression was that those problems were something that were already known, that is, the crimes. But specifically, as far as I can recall, we discussed the appointment of number 16 to the position of brigade commander. And I remember that Mr. Simatovic made a comment to the effect, Which fool had appointed him to the position of commander when he's incapable of leading such a large unit? He's capable of leading a smaller unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the conclusion or decision made at that meeting among Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mr. Simatovic and number 25? My apologies; I mean number 14.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This gentleman, number 14, said that they in Belgrade were not competent, they did not have the authority to appoint or replace commanders. It was the commander, General Mladic, who had that competence. And after that, he went to another office and called up General Mladic by phone. And while he was talking to General Mladic, he called Mr. -- the gentleman under number 9, that is number 9, to come and talk to Mr. Mladic as well. I am not familiar with the contents of that conversation, but later on, Mr. 9 told me briefly what General Mladic had told him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please recount that to us here today.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. 9, when he returned from that other office, he was visibly irritated, and on the way back, he told me that General Mladic had yelled over the phone and had criticised him and said, "What are you looking for in Belgrade? Your place is in number 3, and go back there. What are you looking for in Belgrade? What business have you in Belgrade?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when number 16 was arrested by members of the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was arrested in the summer of 1992. I don't know the exact date, but sometime during the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did number 16 give you a message regarding his arrest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He passed on the message, and he asked me to inform his people in Belgrade to try and save him, to get him out of prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he used the phrase "his people," what did you take that to mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His message was that I inform Frenki that he had been arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attempt to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went there and tried to get in touch with Mr. Frenki. So I did go to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was it you attempted to get in touch with Frenki Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to find him in the building of the MUP of Serbia, but as he wasn't there, I waited for a while across the road in the prefab building that I referred to a moment ago. And while I was waiting for him possibly to appear, some younger men in camouflage uniform who were in that same building told me that Mr. Jovica Stanisic was just coming out of the building and that it would be a good idea for me to brief him about the problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go over to Mr. Stanisic and discuss the problem with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went out of this prefab building and while Mr. Stanisic was waiting for a car to pick him up in front of the MUP building, I approached him. I introduced myself, I said who I was, where I was coming from, and I told him that number 16 had been arrested and that he had asked for assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He first asked me, since he wasn't quite sure what the exact name of the person was, because I only mentioned his nickname, and then he asked me whether he was from that town in which he had been born and for me to tell him his proper name. So I told him his first and last name, and then he said -- he asked me what I thought, who was behind the arrest, and I said that I thought that the League of Communist movement of Yugoslavia was behind it. And he said they've touched into a wasp -- hornet nest and I will now send a telex telling them to release him immediately. So he went back to the building he had just come out of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he used the phrase "they have really touched into a hornet's nest," what did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he meant, but I saw that he didn't like what he heard from me, that this man had been arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return to the municipality marked as number 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was number 16 released from prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was released some ten days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I now ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 476, tab 13.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I could note for the Court, there are actually two copies of the same document in the package provided to the Chamber and the parties in the courtroom. There are some inaccuracies in this document, and the witness was asked to identify which portions of the document he thought were inaccurate, and they have been marked by drawing a line underneath those sections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the first time you saw this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I saw the document was in December 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you just summarise for us the contents of the document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to the contents of the document, they talk about the negative phenomena that affected morale and what was going on in the command of the unit under number 19. And among other things, in a part of the document this group of 30 men is referred to in a positive light, the men that came from Serbia, but later on it says that those people committed criminal acts, and of course the worst crime is also mentioned, the one that took place in the place under number 4. And at the end of the document, mention is made of the steps to be taken in future to prevent these negative phenomena that affected morale and to raise the morale of the unit to a higher level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first saw this document, was it considered a secret document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was considered to be a secret document. Later on, this document was discussed at the Assembly meeting of the municipality under number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, several days ago did you take a copy of this document and draw lines under those portions of it which you believe to be inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The remainder of the document that's not underlined, based upon your personal knowledge, are those sections all accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd now ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 476, tab 14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once again, if I could direct your attention to the signature page. Do you recognise the signature of the person attesting to the stenographic notes of an interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is there anything materially inaccurate in that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there's nothing essentially incorrect. No material inaccuracies to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after number 16 was released from prison, did he remain in the area of number 3 or did he leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He left straight away, left the area and went back home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the fall of 1992, was it discussed whether or not to bring him back to the area or request that he return to the area to once again resume his involvement in the military activity in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that request conveyed to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the request was conveyed to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who conveyed that request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I conveyed that request to him over the phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he put any condition upon his return to the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. He said that if the corps commander wanted him to go back to the area, then he would like me to send a letter to the MUP of Serbia, "and if I am granted permission, then I would come with a group of people. " That's what he said. "Because I don't want to have any unpleasantness over there, for anybody to arrest me or things like that, mistreat me."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was such a letter drafted and sent to the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After consultations and discussions, a decision was taken to write a letter to that effect, requesting his return and the group of men volunteers, and that kind of letter was sent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the author? Who sent -- who was the author of the letter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That letter was written after the Crisis Staff decision was reached of municipality number 3, and the president of the Crisis Staff, the man under number 9, signed the letter, and the letter was sent on to the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who delivered the letter to the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally took the letter and handed it over there to the people from the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which specific person did you hand the letter to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I handed the letter to Mr. Milan Prodanic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention now to the person identified as number 24 on the list of names of tab 3. What involvement or what part did he play in this request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he -- on that day, he scheduled a meeting with the man, which means that when I arrived in Belgrade, I phoned him up and we first met in his office. And later on, Mr. Prodanic arrived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after Mr. Prodanic arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We sat around chatting, discussing the letter, and he asked me to go to the building of the MUP of Serbia with him, to accompany him there. So I went, carrying the letter with me. It was towards evening when we went to the MUP of Serbia building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The MUP of Serbia has several different smaller parts to it. What particular part of the MUP of Serbia did you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we went to the department for state security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when you arrived at the -- or went to the department of state security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was told that they would consider our request and that they would try to give a positive answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when number 16 did return to the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The pace of examination is somewhat too fast. It's very difficult to follow. Could we go back to tab 13 for a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is the event, the massacre included in the indictment, included in this document? And if yes, could we find the relevant passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I can draw the Court's attention to page 2 of that document. The last paragraph, beginning with, "Fifth, the fact that criminals..." And if I could then draw your attention down to the sentence beginning, "The massive arrests and isolation of Croats and Muslims followed..." And if you continue on through that passage, it talks about the location identified as number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can take you back to the office of the state security. Can I ask you to identify all of the people who you met in the state security office to whom you made this request.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in addition to Mr. Prodanic, I met another gentleman whose name was Fica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had you met him prior to that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you were telling us about -- or let me just re-ask the question. Did number 16 return to the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And what happened when he returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he returned, there was an offensive in which he took part with some other men, and what happened was that -- actually what happened was the cause of his trial, why him and the group were tried. All the things that we saw in 13, mentioned in tab 13.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did other men from outside the area also rejoin him in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, a small group arrived with him from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how large was that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There might have been about 20 men. I can't tell you the exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 476, tab 15, and my question to you is: Have you seen the document before, and do you recognise the signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen the document, and I do recognise the signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you summarise what the document or what the letter refers to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as it says here, this is a certificate certifying that five Motorola radio sets of the Radius P-210 type - and then the serial numbers are quoted - and two reserve batteries, one stationary Motorola battery charger --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I might interrupt you. In the event that the specific contents might identify you, can I ask you, does the document refer to property or equipment that was loaned to the municipality by the Republic of Serbia Ministry of Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to correct you on a small point here. Equipment from the MUP of Serbia which was used in this formation under number 19, that military formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was equipment lent by the MUP of Serbia to the now army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness now be shown Prosecution Exhibit 476, tab 16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I could ask you to take a look at the signature page on this document and tell us whether you recognise the signature attesting to the stenographic notes of an interview with that person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise the signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document refers to a meeting with various military officers and a man from the MUP of Serbia. Were you present for at least a portion Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of this meeting referred to in these stenographic notes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present for a portion of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Milan Prodanic the person from the MUP of Serbia who was represented at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything materially inaccurate about the contents of those stenographic notes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, there is nothing that is materially inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can now draw your attention to late October or early November of 1992. Did you attend a meeting in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the meeting that you mentioned a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a specific question about that meeting. Was the subject of number 16 once again discussed between the people at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a discussion about what would be -- what would be done if he once again began to commit crimes and cause problems in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I heard was that when they said good-bye, in parting Mr. Prodanic asked this other man who signed his name to the document that if the man under number 16 were to make any problems whatsoever, that he would take him back to Serbia that very moment; and his answer was, well, there are no problems with him for the time being, and number 16 stayed in our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could ask to go into private session for the next brief portion of testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: B-1244, we are back now in public session, open session. I'd ask the final topic for you to deal with is, can you tell us what you know about the means of supplying diesel oil and fuel to your municipality -- the municipality during the latter part of the war, 1993 to 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, fuel was obtained from the then Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and what I know is that in a short period of time, it was also procured from the Croats in Herceg-Bosna, but for a very short period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the period of time when there was an embargo, were -- was the municipality still receiving fuel from the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There's the matter of these exhibits, Mr. Groome, before you go any further. At the moment, they've been admitted, many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are they to be under seal is the question, and if so, which ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it wasn't our intention -- it was our intention only to put the first three under seal. It appears that the witness -- it's obvious to all of us here in the Chamber that the witness is concerned about -- that the other ones will reveal the location where he's from and thereby reveal his identity. I would ask at this juncture they be placed under seal. After the witness completes his testimony, I will speak to him in greater detail more specifically about his concerns around perhaps raise it again with the Chamber the possibility of making some of these at least, or redacted versions of them, public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now. Cross-examination after the adjournment. Twenty minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, Witness B-1244, if during this cross-examination at any stage you think an answer is one which could reveal your identity, then ask to go into private session and we will consider it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You know the rules, Mr. Milosevic. Any questions to do with the identity of this witness or the municipality or the list of people that you have at tab 3, any of those, go into private session and we'll deal with them in that way. By doing so, it does not mean that we are not listening, of course, to the evidence, and it's being heard, but that part will have to be in private session. Yes. Yes. The registry quite rightly have asked me to remind you that because of this -- and Witness B-1244, both of you, there has to be a pause between question and answer. So could you make sure that his light is off before you answer. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope, in view of these remarks that you have just made now, Mr. May, that you will give me a little more time in view of the fact that you see even these technical requirements take time. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. 1244, you're a native of Bosnia and Herzegovina, are you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent your whole life over there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the war you were there also, were you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You held a responsible post in your place of residence, which I will not mention because we have agreed not to mention it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you have a specific agreement with the side represented by Mr. Groome, or arrangement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think this matter should be dealt with in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true and correct that the Serbs of your municipality - I don't want to mention the name of the municipality - I think Mr. Groome said that the municipality was listed under --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, number 3. So it is a municipality in Bosnia and Herzegovina at any rate. And is it true that in February 1992, at a meeting of the Assembly, that they founded the Serb municipality of number 3, to put it that way; is that right? Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, why did the Serbs set up their own municipal administration?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was because the political circumstances were such and there was the danger of burgeoning Croatian nationalism on the other hand and the creation of a Croatian state. And in Bosnia, this nationalism spilled over into Bosnia with the formation of the fundamentalist, or at least that's how it appeared at the time, the fundamentalist Party of Democratic Action. And the Serbs, in order to protect their own rights, decided to take the step.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, had there already been cases in which Croatian forces had stormed into the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina and taken control of certain places and engaged -- did the Muslim fundamentalist forces engage in various military activities around your municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, there were, in the immediate vicinity west of my own municipality, instances of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, is it true that the decision to set up the Serb municipality of number 3, as we've been calling it and listing it here, is it true that the decision was taken by the legally elected municipal deputies from that same municipality and then also from three other municipalities as well, neighbouring ones? And I think -- I don't think they're on this list, but I assume you know the ones I'm referring to. If you want us to go back into private session, I can tell you the names of those three municipalities. We can do that. It will take a second, but I don't think there's any need. I'm sure the witness must be aware of what I'm talking about. Isn't that right, Mr. 1244?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, at that time, that is to say the period of time during which the Serb municipality was set up in the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina, how many Serbs, refugees, among other things, from Western Slavonia, for example, and from other parts and regions as well passed through that same municipality or decided to stay in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the exact number, but there were many columns which would pass by, coming in from Western Slavonia from time to time. Most of them passed by, and a small portion of them stayed on. But I do know that they passed by, and I do know that the locals organised some food and drink for them during their temporary stay, and then they continued on their journey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they showed them some care and attention, solidarity, and so on, and most of them left, carried along their way, but some of them stayed on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that you were able to talk to many of them. Am I right in assuming that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they tell you? Why did they have to leave their homes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, their stories were deeply shattering, moving. They said that they had to leave their homes for the most part under pressure from the National Guards Corps in Croatia. They called them the Ustashas, and they said it was because of the Ustashas that they had had to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did they call them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the people they called Ustashas, who were these?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as time went on, we began to refer to them the same way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, apart from the attacks that you confirmed happened in part of the territory of your municipality, tell me, before the decision was taken to set up that particular municipality, was there any strong shelling around the surrounding villages in the area by these enemy forces precisely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my area, I don't recall any shelling, but yes, you could hear explosions further off across the Sava River. You could hear the reverberation of those explosions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, then, that there was artillery fire opened from the territory of Croatia across the Sava River and that it was targeted towards certain areas on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, specifically your municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not aware of it having taken place in the area of my municipality. As far as I heard, it was to the west of my municipality. As to my own municipality, I don't remember any artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far to the west of your municipality? How far west?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps 30 to 40 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there any killed and wounded as a result?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I heard at the time, yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So within your family was anybody killed or wounded, any of your family members, during this shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, I did have casualties in my family, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who caused them to be victims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Croatian and Muslim military formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they military men or civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, both; some were military, some were civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that already at that time the detachments had been organised and weapons -- and armed, those formations called the National Guards Corps, the Croatian National Guards Corps and the HOS; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true that the Party of Democratic Action in particular, the leading party on the Muslim side, that it too was organised and armed within the frameworks of the Patriotic League, the so-called Patriotic Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. League of Peoples from the Green Berets and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the founding of the Serb municipal administration in the municipality we're discussing, was that actually a response to an already organised, armed movement on the Croatian and Muslim extremist side and the events linked to the suffering of people -- of the people in Western Slavonia and in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In my opinion, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that already a month later, on the 28th of March, 1992, a new session of the Municipal Assembly was convened and held when you received an important function, post? And I'm talking about the area of municipality number 3 and three other municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that at that time when you came to take up your post, which was in March 1992, that no Serb police forces existed at all at that time? There weren't any; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, new Serb police forces did not exist, if I can call them that, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those days that we have referred to, had the Republika Srpska already been proclaimed within Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in the course of the month of April 1992, up until the second half of May, was the Yugoslav People's Army still the only official and legal armed force within the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in a part of Posavina, the Posavina region that we are discussing, among other areas, there was the so-called 17th Tactical Group of the JNA? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of the reserve JNA force, did you have a position within that 17th Tactical Group, a smaller unit of that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the reserve force within the 17th Tactical Group was organised into four detachments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Groome asked you yesterday two questions, one after another, and I'll combine them. He asked you about the composition of the members of those four detachments, and you said that they were composed of local inhabitants; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then he went on to ask you where did the equipment and weapons come from, and you answered also from local sources, that is, from JNA warehouses nearby; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those four detachments consisted of locals, and the origin of the weapons was also local. Isn't that right, Mr. 1244?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a military conscript, you received call-up papers from the Municipal Secretariat of National Defence, and according to your assignments, you were attached to a particular detachment which was also part of the 17th Tactical Group of the JNA at the time, wasn't it? I won't mention which one it was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was in February 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, like many others, you were drafted and required to attend military exercises; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, is it true that after the withdrawal of the JNA from Bosnia and Herzegovina, in the formation sense the same organisational structure was retained, only the names of the units were changed and the command officers. A moment ago, we established that the four detachments consisted of locals, that their weapons were also from local sources, they were under JNA command for as long as the JNA existed. When the JNA withdrew, they remained in their own area as part of the army of Republika Srpska that was in the process of being formed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that on the 17th of April, while the JNA were still in the area, the commander of the 17th Tactical Group ordered that major facilities and institutions in your municipality be placed under control, that control be taken of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now tell me, please, since a question is being repeatedly referred to here regarding the takeover of power, tell me, was this done in order to take over power by the Serbs in your municipality, that is municipality number 3, or was the intention to ensure the normal functioning of public utilities, economic institutions, installations and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was done with those intentions in mind and that idea in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the commander of the JNA tactical group sought to ensure the normal functioning of public utilities, the economy, and other important institutions for the municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He asked the local civilian authorities to organise those public services.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that within the territory of that municipality, your municipality, both Croatian forces and Muslim forces had already organised themselves within their own TO independently of the JNA and as part of units such as the Patriotic League, the Green Berets, the HVO, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You speak of events of the 17th of April, saying that a group of volunteers participated, some 50 of them; is that right? According to your statement, 30 of them came from Serbia and the rest were young men from the territory of your municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As Mr. Groome is using these 30 men and explaining them as being a special unit from Serbia, is it true that 28 of those 30 were -- I don't know whether I may mention the town in Serbia, it's not on the list here -- and that they were volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since the JNA was still in existence, were they volunteers in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The very next day after their arrival, they joined into the existing military units and became part of those units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To make this quite clear, when various abstracts are picked out of context, the mosaic may be wrong. So this group of volunteers from one municipality was not a unit of the state security from Serbia but volunteers of a particular party that joined the JNA as volunteers. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a rather complicated question. They came as volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party and were immediately included in the military unit that was under JNA command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking you. And later on, when the JNA withdrew, they were volunteers in the army of Republika Srpska. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So whichever time period we are referring to, that group was a group of volunteers that had either reported to the JNA when the JNA existed in the area or to the army of Republika Srpska later on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were no special unit of any kind of the state security of Serbia, were they, Mr. 1244? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. While they were in the territory of this municipality, they were, up until the 18th of May, part of the JNA. And after the 18th of May, they were part of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am saying this because the Serbian Radical Party claims that it always sent volunteers either to the JNA or to the army of Republika Srpska or to the army of Republika Srpska Krajina, that it never formed its own separate units. And is that true regarding the territory of your municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were either volunteers to the JNA or to the army of Republika Srpska; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Heading this volunteer unit, according to what you said, was a certain person, number 16, the person number 16; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: While he was in the territory of that municipality, he was within the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am saying this because I wish to emphasise because I understand that Mr. Groome is endeavouring to represent him as if he represented the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Serbia, whereas in fact he was a volunteer in the army of Republika Srpska. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that that person had an official ID of anybody from the Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any official ID on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke yesterday about a meeting you had in Belgrade with Franko Simatovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like us to explain that in somewhat greater detail. Were you ever invited by him to come to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you say you met him twice, did he issue any order to you of any kind or give you any kind of instructions in connection with anything at all? There's no need for me to be more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly? There was a group of some 20 of people from your area being trained in the Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But Eastern Slavonia was still SO Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja; isn't that right? That's how it was known. Or was it already the Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what it was formally called, but I know geographically speaking it was the area of Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you wanted to visit those men who were there being trained, is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you went, taking the only route you could, that is via Serbia, and you dropped in at the Ministry of Internal Affairs to ask someone to help you go there, to take you there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Groome spoke about that as if you wanted them to take care of your transportation, but from what you said, I gather that they told you that somebody would be going in that direction shortly and that you can follow that person to reach the destination you wanted to reach; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on that same day, not the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they didn't transport you there, but you just followed a vehicle that was going in that direction anyway; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was when you saw Franko Simatovic. You saw him travelling in that direction, wearing civilian clothing and going about his business, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on you explained that you stopped by a house near to Ilok where he got out because he had some talks or something to do, and they saw to it that they give you somebody to escort you to the camp so that you could find the local people who were attending training there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't have any knowledge about any links he might have had with the camp, because he stayed on in a house that had nothing to do with the camp and you were given somebody else to drive you off or, rather, to show you the way to reach the camp so that you could see these people of yours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He gave me somebody who took me there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was helping out a colleague in that kind of way. He helped you find your way to visit the people you knew over there in the camp in Republika Srpska Krajina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a gesture on his part following the request of this other man, number 13, who gave me the idea of doing that and asked me to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This number 13 was a functionary of your municipality in Bosnia-Herzegovina, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, it was at his suggestion that you went to visit these people and you asked your colleagues to show you the way, where it was located; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
